## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Fó shuō sān-zhuǎn fǎ-lún jīng* is a single-fascicle Táng-period 唐 translation of the First Sermon, focusing on its analytical structure as the *three turnings* (parijñā / prahāṇa / sākṣātkaraṇa) of the four noble truths — twelve elements in all (3 × 4). It is a parallel of [T109](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0109) (An Shigao). The Chinese title 三轉 ("three turnings") preserves the Mūlasarvāstivāda-tradition's analytical articulation more clearly than the older T109.

**Abstract**

T110 was produced during Yìjìng's post-695 translation career; the defensible bracket 695–713 is recorded in the frontmatter. The Indic source is presumed lost. The text is one of Yìjìng's many short *Mūlasarvāstivāda-Vinaya*-affiliated sūtras and shows the classical post-Xuánzàng Tang Buddhist register.
